key_insight: MethylVI is a deep probabilistic model that disentangles biological methylation states from technical noise in single-cell bisulfite sequencing, enabling accurate denoising, imputation and uncertainty-aware downstream analyses. It models read-level methylation measurements with a generative (variational) framework tailored to the data's coverage and overdispersion.
problem_solved: Single-cell bisulfite sequencing data are extremely sparse, noisy and coverage-variable, making it hard to recover true methylation patterns, correct batch/technical effects, and perform reliable downstream tasks (clustering, differential methylation). MethylVI addresses these challenges by explicitly modelling technical and biological variability in a principled probabilistic way.
method: Probabilistic deep generative model (variational autoencoder) that represents each cell with latent biological and technical factors.
Observations modelled with a (beta-)binomial-like likelihood that accounts for per-site coverage and overdispersion so methylated-read counts are handled appropriately.
Amortized variational inference for scalable learning, producing posterior estimates for denoised methylation, imputation and calibrated uncertainty for downstream analyses.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a domain-specific example of combining likelihood engineering with deep latent-variable models to recover signal from extremely sparse, noisy biological measurements; enables robust, uncertainty-aware single-cell methylome analyses and can inspire similar approaches in other sparse genomic modalities.
visual_elements: Schematic of the model: encoder mapping raw methylated/read counts and covariates to latent biological and technical factors, and decoder predicting methylation probabilities (with beta-binomial iconography).
Before/after heatmap: raw sparse methylation matrix vs denoised/imputed methylation values to show signal recovery.
Latent-space embedding (UMAP/tSNE) colored by cell type and batch to illustrate batch correction and biological separation.
Calibration/uncertainty plot: predictive credible intervals or error vs coverage showing improved confidence estimates and imputation accuracy.
paper_title: Probabilistic modelling of single-cell bisulfite sequencing data with MethylVI
paper_authors: Ethan Weinberger, Wei Qiu, Wei Tian, Qiurui Zeng, Can Ergen
